chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ays ibn al-Qasim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about eating with the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian. He said: 'If it was from your food, then perform ablution, and there is no problem with it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating with Jews, Christians, and Magians according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of sharing meals with the People of the Book (Jews, Christians, and Zoroastrians) by linking it to ritual purity. The ruling specifies that if the food originates from one's own provision, performing ablution (*wudu*) before eating renders the meal acceptable, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ritual cleanliness in social interactions with non-Muslims. This highlights the distinction between the intrinsic purity of the food source and the ritual state of the eater.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ays Bin Al Qasim who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the meals of the Jews and the Christians, and the Magians. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was from your meals, so perform ablution, and there is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from ‘Is ibn al-Qasim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, about eating with the Jews, Christians and Zoroastrians. He (the Imam) said, ’If the food belongs to you then make wudu (wash) and eat with them; it is not unlawful.’”
